reviewEvidence.approvalScope: Complete authored tabletop procedure; no complete runtime adapter or human balance claim.

completeSharedRules.title: Authority, access and cost
completeSharedRules.wording: The selected ordinary identity and its actual classAccess row control school, rank, minimum class level and base RP. Preserve the entire classAccess object, every catalog/Core original, book binding, placeholder, absent/null distinction and additionalRpCost. Enough RP does not grant access or repertoire. An already completed explicit ordinary-spell access exception, such as the actual Druid Circle always-prepared table, retains its real acquisition/rank/preparation gates once its matching payload passes exact review. Record that particular grant and use its actual class progression/cost; do not rewrite ordinary classAccess, infer a new variant from a same-named class power, or approve a pending class feature here. Rank costs remain 0/2/3/5/7/10/13/17/21/26 for ranks 0–9, with the actual class engine, discounts, Dissonance surcharge and additional/maintenance costs separately applied. Oracle Revelations remain RC techniques; a same-named class, ancestry or recipe permission is not this ordinary spell. No default upcast or cantrip level scaling is added. Every direction below is authoring authority only; every existing source operational:null and pending status remains untouched until separate exact review.

completeSharedRules.title: Actual casting transaction
completeSharedRules.wording: Use the selected source Action, Bonus Action, Reaction or longer casting time and actual V/S/F or M/F requirements. V requires the caster's own presently usable voice; recordings are not V. S and a real permitted focus obey the existing hand/access rules. Unpriced M/F permits the actual focus alternative and creates no invented costly/consumed material fee. Explicit physical substrates below are real target/work prerequisites, not inferred M costs. Observable legality is checked before commitment; hidden immunity/type/meaning does not become free diagnosis. At commitment spend the actual action/resources and update actual cast/cadence history before the existing counterspell chain; a countered, missed or resisted committed cast refunds nothing. Concentration begins under the existing rule and can end the old concentration even when the new cast is countered. Long casting uses actual uninterrupted work and governing interruption/Ready rules. No successful spell roll authenticates an asserted object, voice, teacher, corpse or world permission.

completeSharedRules.title: Native rolls and damage
completeSharedRules.wording: Spell attacks use the actual owner's spell attack modifier versus AC: natural 1 misses, natural 20 hits and doubles damage dice of that attack, not flat modifiers or later ticks. Saves are binary total-versus-spell-DC, with no natural-die degree shift. A specified examination is an INT (Investigation) task against the creating caster's snapshotted spell DC: use Core degrees/natural shifts, then collapse Success/Critical Success versus Failure/Critical Failure unless an entry supplies distinct outcomes. For one simultaneous area effect, snapshot geometry and eligible targets before damage, roll each stated shared damage expression once, then apply each recipient's save and actual type defenses independently. Half damage floors each typed component once at the stated save stage. Follow the existing reduction, immunity/resistance/vulnerability, temporary/form buffer, actual HP loss, Wound, death and concentration pipeline. No descriptive Damage/Healing/Control tag supplies an additional attack, damage, healing or condition.

completeSharedRules.disposition: KEEP; NEW explicit use where source timing is absent
completeSharedRules.title: Clocks
completeSharedRules.wording: A bare hostile one-round rider ends at the end of the target's next future regular turn, excluding an in-progress turn at application; a bare self/ally one-round benefit ends at the start of the caster's next future regular turn. N hostile rounds use the Nth such target end; N buff rounds use the Nth caster start. Outside initiative, those are 6N elapsed seconds. Keep the registered clock through initiative changes using the existing virtual-clock adapter; extra turns do not create expiry/tick opportunities. A NEW duration expressed in minutes/hours below uses an absolute elapsed deadline from completed resolution, including an absolute 60-second deadline for “1 minute”; the one-minute means neither an extra initial tick nor reset when initiative starts. Repeated round damage expressly uses future target regular-end checkpoints and its printed finite count, not one immediate tick plus that count. End-turn ticks/repeat saves precede their scheduled end-turn expiry; start expiry precedes voluntary actions. Suppression pauses eligibility/effect, not deadlines; scheduled suppressed ticks are spent, never queued. Entries that expressly use a named trigger instead of a generic clock keep that trigger.

completeSharedRules.title: Multiplicity, effect identity and present state
completeSharedRules.wording: Keep the existing strongest same-stat flat bonus, same-family cover arbitration, advantage/disadvantage cancellation and one eligible bonus-die spell per roll. Independent class exceptions retain their exact scopes; this is not a universal strongest-effect rule. NEW default for these previously uncompleted spells: one active instance per caster per ordinary spell ID, unless a row expressly permits more; a successfully resolved replacement ends that caster's prior instance, but an illegal/countered attempt does not replace a nonconcentration instance. Different casters retain separate source records, clocks and restrictions; identical numeric bonuses never add. A current complete record is required for every competing effect. Instantaneous completed consequences are not active-instance stock. An entry explicitly limiting waiting triggers counts only its stated waiting state; its spent playback phase never refills or occupies a waiting slot. Continual Flame explicitly permits separate paid anchors, with only its per-anchor limit; do not impose the default one-caster limit on it. Loss, repair, transfer, suppression or a new database ID cannot renew an already consumed mark, scheduled tick, trigger, command budget or source resource. Removal of one source does not erase another's independent condition. Any change in actual target/custody state is logged; it is not a new casting.

completeSharedRules.title: Attack/check marks
completeSharedRules.wording: A row expressly saying attack commitment reserves and spends its mark when the beneficiary commits a legal declared attack, before a roll; cancellation after that commitment and a miss do not refund it, while an illegal declaration that never commits does not spend it. Otherwise “next attack/check” marks spend on the next actual qualifying roll, including a miss/failure; unrelated rolls and passive procedures do not consume them. Mark recipients cannot choose to save a mark for a later preferred roll. A next-hit rider spends on the first qualifying hit, even if defenses reduce its damage to zero. Multiple competing next-roll marks eligible for the same event all spend, though only permitted strongest/advantage effects operate. Suppressed marks do not benefit or consume on an event while suppressed, but their deadline continues. Delivery attacks and later attacks consuming a delivered mark are different events.

completeSharedRules.title: Sight, illusions and meaning
completeSharedRules.wording: An image is not an opaque physical barrier, creature, material, light source, safe floor, sound receiver or extra targetable body unless its row expressly creates that thing. Ordinary hearing needs a real acoustic path; sight needs the relevant illumination, range and unobstructed view. Knowing an illusion does not grant sight through a real wall. For visual/audio deceptions below that permit examination, one Action using a currently accessible relevant sense can make the LR-G03 examination; success identifies that cast as illusory for that observer, while failure permits another examination only after genuinely new evidence or method. Conclusive witnessed physical contradiction establishes the applicable false part without a roll. An ally's warning allows examination but does not globally switch every observer to knowing. These procedures do not compel belief, pursuit, an attack, trust or a sale. Current Invisible rules remain: invisibility is not automatic Hidden; observers who know location lose only the special invisibility-derived attack advantage/disadvantage, not unrelated concealment. Language samples reproduce what was heard, not meaning or credentials. Preserve LA's six-second aggregate voluntary-speech budget per numbered round and actual component/oath windows. Spell-created sounds are not the caster's later speech, but original recording speech and the caster's V are real speech.

completeSharedRules.title: Range, targets and geometry
completeSharedRules.wording: Unless a specific row explicitly uses detection without sight, select an actually perceived eligible target or point within the literal Core range and with the existing line of effect. A target can be self within a creature-target range unless the source/row restricts it. “Willing” means current actual consent; an unwilling holder prevents a willing-only object spell without supplying an opposed-roll workaround. Detecting some magic is not necessarily perceiving a creature for targeting it. One target means one physical identity, not every same-named database row. NEW missing cone width is its length at its far end; missing line cross-section is five feet wide and five feet high. All source radii remain radii, not distances added to cast range. Area membership/cover are evaluated from the actual origin at that event; walls are not retroactively removed for a second pass. “Enemies” uses the caster's declared ordinary opposition set, not a supernatural alignment/intent detector. Caster/allies are included in indiscriminate areas. No range is silently replaced by an outside game's value.

completeSharedRules.title: Conditions and hard-control guard
completeSharedRules.wording: Use actual Blinded, Deafened, Frightened, Prone, Restrained, Incapacitated, Paralyzed and Stunned definitions without importing another game. Paralyzed/Incapacitated and other hard Action denial obey the current source-character/target/encounter allowance shared across that owner's effects; only successfully established hard control spends it, once for the effect's full allowed window. A blocked hard portion supplies no invented substitute penalty; independently printed damage, Prone or another separately allowed portion can remain. A spell's repeat save ends only the stated source. Ending laughter, restraint or paralysis does not automatically stand a Prone target. NEW “flee” directions below require actual safe available movement away at the next regular-turn movement opportunity, using existing Speed/cost and leaving Actions to the target; they do not force Dash, expend a Reaction or require deliberate self-harm. If no safe farther legal location exists, no movement is forced and no action is lost. Panicked is explicitly bound only in IL-23, not added as a global condition. Haste's voluntary ending cost is separately addressed in R3-12.

completeSharedRules.title: Movement, falls and body continuity
completeSharedRules.wording: Ordinary movement spends real movement cost and needs nonzero permitted Speed, legal support, actual space and the appropriate locomotion mode; changing a speed or mode does not reset spent cost. A spell-directed extra movement allowance expressly stated below supplies only that finite allowance. Teleportation relocates rather than traverses, does not itself provoke opportunity attacks and does not generically defeat a source that blocks relocation; no route is inferred through planes. Check destination occupancy, whole body/gear geometry and lawful carry/load. Supplying a point is not permission to materialize inside another body. Unsupported endings, launches and lost flight use the existing FallMarker and finite falling resolution, not a new immediate damage tick. Actual transformations retain original identity, own HP/resources, spent state, origin restrictions and body/equipment priority; no new monster sheet, harvest pool, HP refill, gear duplication or size-based ability increase. Actual equipment can be melded only by the stated form procedure, stays real weight/history and is unavailable while melded.

completeSharedRules.title: Summons, corpse assets and commands
completeSharedRules.wording: Each row supplies its actual finite body, attack and lifetime rather than importing a monster. Use printed HP/AC before any new fallback. For the NEW profiles below, creating caster's class level/PB/ability at creation fixes any printed-derived maximum; attacks and saves use that same source owner's currently lawful spell attack/PB, not a transferee's or a monster's sheet. Unless stated, saves add owner's PB, ordinary ability/skill checks add 0, normal vision only, no special damage or condition immunity, no independent equipment proficiency or spellcasting. One such spell-created asset per caster per spell ID; the existing total companion/control budget still binds. Creation grants no free attack or movement. A command uses one Bonus Action on the owner's regular turn through actual visible/audible communication within 60 ft; no telepathy is invented. It acts in the attached phase after that whole turn, shares the owner's one command and one offensive companion/device allowance per numbered round, and has no independent refresh on extra turns. Uncommanded it can only ordinary Dodge and make defensive movement within speed; no automatic pursuit, work or offense. Loss of the channel means no new command, not free autonomy. A complete task needs its real appendages, capacity, instructions and paid time. At 0 HP, expiry, source dismissal (Action) or concentration end where required, the asset ends; summoned apparatus disappears without loot, corpses, ammunition, harvest or salvage. An actual corpse used as fuel retains its original finite matter/history and the stated terminal consumption; no source can reclassify it as newly obtained material. Keep Ranger's genuinely ordinary animal remains distinct from no-resource summons.

completeSharedRules.title: Suppression and trigger ordering
completeSharedRules.wording: An ongoing magical object's target stays the same physical anchor; transfer or repair cannot duplicate/rearm it. Full magical suppression prevents sensing/operation while it lasts and does not queue missed triggers; duration continues. An acoustic silence can block only sound independently of a physically detected trigger. Resolve simultaneous eligible one-shot triggers in creation order then stable cast ID. Consume a triggered use before its payload, even when a later barrier, silence, immunity, cancellation or receiver state prevents useful output. A sound produced by another real spell can be a phonetic trigger if all actual constraints match, but each waiting trigger resolves at most once and cannot recreate itself or another charge. Source death/distance ends a nonconcentration effect only where the source/row says so; it does not refresh it. Suppression does not undo already completed mundane writing, moved matter, healing, damage or superficial preparation. An explicit persistent permanent spell remains a magical effect, not a manufactured item or free rechargeable device.

completeSharedRules.disposition: NEW spell-specific wrapper family; existing costs/cadence kept
completeSharedRules.title: Copying, acceleration, delay and proxies
completeSharedRules.wording: Cantrip Echo, Echo Cast, Quick Cast and Delay Spell are the only new wrapper identities authorized here. None may take itself or any of those four as payload, nor may an already echoed/released payload become a replay source. One payload may receive at most one of these temporal/replay modifications; they do not duplicate Ready or grant an additional Bonus Action, Reaction or full Action. Existing acquired class permissions remain their own exceptions, not automatically folded into this family. Select the actual original casting record, same ordinary source class and native legal access; only that spell's normal Action version with one finite resolution is eligible, excluding long casts, Reactions, Bonus Action spells and ongoing maintenance actions. Repeating a miss or resisted but fully resolved cast permits a fresh legal cast, not copying its damage result; a countered or aborted original is not a replay source. New targets/range/components and current costs/statistics must qualify at the new commitment. No active rider, successful roll, other caster's access, expended item charge or selected resource award is copied for free. Cantrip Echo's row defines one composite ordinary-cast transaction; Echo Cast/Quick Cast/Delay Spell instead have their separately paid arming transactions and later actual payload commitments. Record parent, wrapper, payload, cost, original owner and single-use consumption. No zero-base-cost replay recursively generates resource refunds or unearned casts. A legal fresh payload still resolves its own actual damage and expressly funded healing; this guard prevents copied old awards and recursive new-cast/refund grants, not the payload’s specified new outcome. Resonance Tether changes a legitimate delivery origin only, never the responsible caster or their RP/RC pool.

completeSharedRules.title: Reflection without a new cast
completeSharedRules.wording: Spell Mirror and Soul Mirror intercept only the first actually resolving ordinary spell effect that has exactly their warded creature as its sole direct creature recipient, beneficial or hostile. Area, multitarget, self-only, anchor/object, summoning, channel/ongoing tick and already redirected effects are ineligible. NEW interception/return distinction: a Touch-delivered, healing or willing-recipient spell is eligible for interception when it satisfies the foregoing sole-recipient and scope requirements. The original caster's eligibility to receive the return, including actual consent and creature-type requirements, is tested only after that eligible ward has been spent. An ineligible original caster therefore causes a spent, unsuccessful return and leaves the original recipient, exactly as below. A legal Touch return uses this explicit magical return, not a new physical touch or Action. No rank cap is added; actual protective exceptions can still forbid redirection. After counterspell resolution but before that spell's attack/save/effect, spend the ward once and substitute the original actual caster as recipient only when it is presently a legal recipient under the payload's own type/other eligibility. Classless creatures can be targeted, but no class features are manufactured for them.

READING: on the initial failed save, privately show the caster the actual currently acquired class-feature identities and their complete operative mechanical descriptions, including applicable Base/Arch/Hero/Mystery/Oath selections and genuine passive/active modes. Reveal these as current class mechanics, not a dump of historical source variants or every unselected future option. Current temporarily unusable but genuinely acquired features remain part of that readable roster. NEW the result is one snapshot, not a live feed; suppression/return does not rerun it. It includes the actual class identity necessary to understand a feature, but no independent exact class-level, ability-score, currentHP/RP, remaining-use ledger, prepared-spell list, inventory, oath history or private biography query. An unavoidable inference from legitimately revealed mechanics is ordinary inference. A genuinely established empty class-feature roster can return No Class Features; missing/unclassified records return Indeterminate for that portion instead of inventing an NPC class.

Apply information defenses as they stood for this initial application before suppression. A blocked or contradictory reading is not retried after its defensive feature is suppressed. Protection against information alone need not prevent the separately operative suppression; a defense against the whole actual spell does. Oracle's Burden and the selected intrinsic Oracle Curse retain their actual expressly protected status: this generic class suppression does not strip the Burden to bootstrap suppression of the Curse or its protected effects. In particular, preserve an acquired Soul-Cracked Boon IV's actual direct-divination d2 information result and its real scope; do not invent a random false class sheet. This is not a new exception authorizing a Curse cure.

SUPPRESSION: disable actual active, passive, triggered and activated mechanics whose continuing source is the target's acquired class feature, including actual Base/Arch/Hero abilities, class engines and their real aliases. This covers class Extra Attack, class-casting/command/recovery permissions, class AC/Speed/damage modifiers and continuous class bonuses delivered to real dependents. Resolve aliases as one source, not a surviving second copy. Do not remove earned levels, the ordinary level-derived PB/baseHP/base resource schedule, permanent acquired ability-score increases, ordinary learned skill/tool/language/weapon training, selected feats, ancestry, background, equipment powers or native NPC actions merely because those facts appear on a class sheet. A class-only expertise or proficiency multiplier is suppressed; the underlying ordinary proficiency remains. A feature genuinely supplied independently by an unaffected source remains usable only under that source's own costs and limits. Acquiring a feat through an ASI selection does not turn that feat into a class feature.

The creature retains its ordinary Action, movement and legal mundane options. This is not whole-Action loss merely because its favored attacks/spells are unavailable, and spends no hard-control allowance. It imposes no Stunned/Incapacitated or mandatory wasted Action. No permission to erase a pending entire ordinary Action is added. A previously committed class activation that still requires an unavailable feature to resolve has no suppressed payload, while its real costs stay spent; any expressly independent already-committed spell or physical projectile follows the distinction below. Hard-control components originating from genuinely suppressed class parents cannot act during the interval, but their admission history and endpoints persist; return does not claim again. Actual ordinary control spells already cast through a class casting engine are not themselves erased with that engine.

DEPENDENTS: an already established ordinary spell remains its own ongoing spell application, including actual spells generated by class cards whose operative source supplies the spell interface; losing permission for the next cast does not end an old one. Continuous class modifiers to that spell cease while their feature is suppressed. Actual feature-maintained auras, stances, form benefits, marks and periodic outputs become inoperative, with original clocks and relationship requirements continuing. A Druid class form whose anatomy is actively feature-maintained reverts through the reviewed one-body/equipment procedure during suppression; its still-live original form may resume only if its real duration, concentration, custody and geometry remain legal. No new creation, fullHP body, fresh gear state or re-paid activation is invented. An instantaneous permanent bodily change or completed ordinary material/output is not rolled back.

Existing class-created companion/device bodies and actual items remain present with their real identity, inventory, currentHP, source slots and ending rules; creation is not repeated on return. The suppressed owner's class command permission cannot issue new commands or execute a pending command dependent on it. Capable uncommanded companions retain their real defensive Move/Dodge procedure and attached phase; independent creatures retain actual native agency, without an extra turn. Ordinary spell-granted command permission independent of a suppressed class-only feature remains only if its source expressly supplies it. Ownership, slot reservations, no-duplicate-body histories and shared one-command/one-offense accounting persist. Passive owner-class maximumHP bonuses on dependent creatures are suppressed even if that dependent is elsewhere; it is the feature's continuing output, not a new ranged target or secret roster report.

CAPACITY/ECONOMY: remove suppressible class maximumHP modifiers and recompute using the reviewed separate-record formula; clamp current normalHP downward if necessary, without damage, Wounds, first-fall triggers or concentration checks. Returning capacity gives no HP. Base level-derived resource capacity/identity remains, but a separately suppressible capacity bonus is unavailable. NEW conservation partition for an existing finite resource balance above its temporary operative cap: keep the excess in that same pool's inaccessible reserve, not a second spendable pool. Only the accessible part can be spent by a genuinely independent remaining permission. Gains/refunds must account for both portions against the operative cap, never refill space occupied by reserved units. As capacity actually returns, move still-existing reserved units back only up to that capacity; do not generate new units. If a real source-specific permanent loss removes those units, the reserve cannot restore them. All spending, daily/recharge/recovery/cooldown histories and debt remain. Source-defined cooldown progression continues even when activation is unavailable; missed class-triggered recoveries or pulses are lost, not queued. A feature return is neither a rest nor encounter start. Obligations and already incurred costs are not canceled by suppressing their source.

Ending, actual dispel or suppression of Eye restores only still-present eligible mechanics. It does not reconstruct ended concentration/forms, removed companions, spent entitlements, expired marks or completed lost triggers. Repeated Eye applications are independent same-effect suppression records, no additive penalty; a surviving one keeps its coverage when another ends. An information result already received can be remembered normally and is not erased by later dispel. For ordinary Ready, preparation fixes spell and mode/score/limb-role intent and pays once, while actual legal recipient/limb identity, target point and resulting geometry/item snapshots are selected at legal release under the existing Ready contract. rules.scope: Eight-spell source clocks, ending saves and lifecycle; no new global scheduler.
rules.text: Sixty-second effects run from successful establishment, not prospective concentration; Wind Walk runs 3600 elapsed seconds; Flesh to Stone has no timed endpoint. Expiry wins over any same-time upkeep, resumption or repeat opportunity and consumes its endpoint once. Suppression never pauses any clock or queues missed benefits, healing, movement or commands. Genuine recipient END saves for Petrify Limb continue while its expression is suppressed or its part is temporarily unmatched. Use the recipient's actual regular END, including an underway eligible END after admission; extra turns do not supply additional regular-END saves. For an actually owner-attached creature use its genuine attached-phase END; if that regular owner turn supplies no execution phase, use that owner's real END for a spell-ending save only. This fallback is NEW and only for Petrify Limb; it grants no body, owner, Action or command. Persist source/recipient/real-turn marker receipts across controller or schedule changes. If genuinely outside initiative with no actual recurring phase, make a spell-ending-only CON save after each completed six-second interval anchored to admission; entering a real schedule cancels the competing virtual endpoint and uses only future real ENDs, without replaying any prior elapsed interval. Actual encounter/schedule transitions are director/world events, not an actor-selected resource reset. Death and source expiry are processed before any endpoint save. A success permanently ends the source; later suppression exit does not reapply it.

rules.scope: Actual body, gear, part and placement records; not new creature profiles.

rules.scope: Only the defense/score components expressly given by these spells.
rules.text: Calculate the actual compatible armor/form formula, then strongest applicable spell-family flat AC. completeOriginalQuestion.recommendationAndConsequences: Recommend A with explicit unresolved profile prerequisites: body guide supplies Tiny throughLarge only; no invented Huge/Gargantuan dimensions. Continuous1inch passage is not whole-body voluntary endpoint fit, no liquid/solid bypass, no split scouts, no new resistance, and no arbitrary cargo capture.
completeOriginalQuestion.scope: Local clearance/profile permission; missing size interfaces remain visible.

questions.selectedAnswer: No invented size ceiling; require the actual root-body/carrying/meld/placement profile. Continuous one-inch opening permits transit, not splitting, passing solid walls/liquid or ending where the full body cannot fit.
questions.reasonAndTradeoff: Larger sizes remain eligible in principle but their unprovided end-to-end fixtures stay conditional. Gaseous Form remains its separate Fly10/concentration procedure.

completeOriginalQuestion.question: Preserve actual explicit Corruption-protection restriction and broad eligible nonmagical damage, distinct from physical B/P/S including magical. Demonstrate mixed typed packets and suppressed/removed strongest-AC source revealing a weaker source without restoring prior damage.

questions.selectedAnswer: Greater Stoneflesh tests actual nonmagical provenance with the explicit Corruption exclusion; Ironskin tests B/P/S type regardless of magical flag. AC and resistance are independent, with suppressed stronger AC revealing a weaker still-live one.
questions.reasonAndTradeoff: Mixed types must not turn a nonphysical component into physical or erase original source properties. Actual damage sources/rolls are mandatory in positive fixture claims.

completeOriginalQuestion.question: Explicitly classify partial Petrify Limb versus full Petrified, Gaseous/Wind Walk and actual Alter Self anatomy. A cosmetic appearance does not bypass the actual form block; concentration displacement happens before blocked replacement. Include own voluntary ending and genuine temporary suppression.

questions.selectedAnswer: Block new full forms, new size and actual Alter Self modes, including physical appearance adaptation. Exclude mere images and the expressly named partial/full petrification condition applications. Let actual form endings happen before any prohibited replacement is tested.
questions.reasonAndTradeoff: No permanent preservation of a current shape and no generic transmutation immunity. No hidden block becomes a free diagnostic.

completeOriginalQuestion.question: Arm mode says the limb is fixed immobile, yet a dual-purpose limb must get only its selected manipulator OR locomotor mechanical result. For anatomy requiring that same arm for walking/climbing, distinguish the selected mechanical outcome from actual immobility consequences. Supply a coherent role/dependency rule rather than simultaneously asserting fixed immobility and fully functional movement through it. Do not invent a qualifying creature anatomy merely for a positive case.

questions.selectedAnswer: Select role-restricted articulated stone, not immobile whole appendage plus magically unrelated claim of normal motion. Disabled manipulator actions cannot be re-described as locomotion; independent real gait may remain. Locomotor role halts only modes genuinely requiring the part.
questions.reasonAndTradeoff: A complete actual dual-role anatomy/procedure is still required to evaluate a positive special-anatomy case. The ordinary human arm and actual required Hawk wing are distinct supplied examples.

completeOriginalQuestion.question: Map admission, genuine future/affected current END saves, attached/no-phase cadence, severed part identity and target death. A saved/blocked new cast cannot replace the old limb source; a missing current limb is not healed by suppression or ending.

questions.selectedAnswer: Initial save then regular END, including a currently underway eligible END; real attached END or owner-END save-only fallback if no execution phase. Record completed markers, preserve deadline through suppression/transformation and process expiry first. Same original creature supplies saves for a separated part.
questions.reasonAndTradeoff: This explicitly local extension supplies no companion or new phase. Lost part is not restored by success, suppression or ending.

completeOriginalQuestion.question: Current exact holder rules and continuous meld ceilings govern. Remove the pending Eye of Judgement reserve import unless separately and expressly selected for a real identified resource. Demonstrate CON floor5->7 with currentHP3 unchanged, actual paid heal7, suppression clamp5, resumption max7/current5, final removal and no loss-as-damage/Wound. A source whose RP is fixed by class level has no invented score-dependent RP balance.

Verify support/carrying changes at admission/suppression/end, overlapping condition sources and exact dispel scope. Include full versus partial actual daily intake intervals without resetting shortage/rest/death schedules; no implicit time stasis.

questions.reasonAndTradeoff: Permanent condition is not a temporary alternate HP body, object durability profile or temporal stasis. Actual severing, death and support failure need their own authority.

Real mass/gear and body-size changes must revalidate every swept segment. Suppressed-live and final-ended pending placement must stay distinct.

cards.name: Arcane Recovery
cards.duration: Instantaneous during a completed short rest
cards.effect: Arcane Recovery. Tags: base, passive, resonance. Once between long rests when you complete a short rest, restore RP equal to half your Wizard class level rounded up, never above your normal maximum. This is RP recovery, not a second pool, and cannot trigger spell-cast, Refrain or Dissonance effects.

source.originalText: Arcane Recovery: Once per day during a short rest, recover RP equal to half your Wizard level (rounded up), up to your normal maximum.

cards.name: Spell Scribing
cards.effect: Spell Scribing. Tags: base, passive, spellbook. Copying a legal found Wizard spell into your spellbook requires 1 hour and 25 gp of inks and components per spell rank, treating rank 0 as rank 1 for this calculation, instead of the pilot baseline 2 hours and 50 gp. Level-up spells remain free.

source.originalText: Spell Scribing: Copy spells into your spellbook at half the normal cost and time.

cards.name: Arcane Bolt
cards.effect: Arcane Bolt. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, universal, damage. Make a Wizard spell attack. On a hit deal S d6 + M force damage. Arcane Bolt is an always-prepared class matrix once acquired and uses the normal first-distinct-matrix and Refrain rules.

source.originalText: Arcane Bolt: Launch a bolt of pure arcane energy that deals force damage to a single target.

cards.name: Minor Conjuration
cards.frequency: At will while RP remains; one object at a time
cards.effect: Minor Conjuration. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, conjuration. Create one nonmagical unattended object that fits inside a 1-foot cube, weighs no more than 10 pounds and is made of common nonvaluable material such as wood, cloth, clay, iron or glass. It cannot be food, poison, currency, a spell component with listed cost, ammunition with special properties or a functional complex mechanism. Creating another dismisses the first.

source.originalText: Minor Conjuration: Create a temporary, small inanimate object that lasts for 1 hour.

cards.name: Arcane Insight
cards.effect: Arcane Insight. Tags: base, passive, knowledge. Gain proficiency in Arcana, or expertise if already proficient. When examining an active magical effect, spell residue, magic item or arcane construction, you may make an Intelligence (Arcana) check to determine its broad school, function or unusual matrix behavior. The Director sets the normal knowledge DC; failure supplies no invented fact.

source.originalText: Arcane Insight: Identify magical effects and items with greater accuracy than non-wizards.

cards.name: Matrix Efficiency
cards.effect: Matrix Efficiency. Tags: base, passive, matrix. Your normal full daily Spell Matrix preparation time is reduced from 1 hour to 45 minutes. This does not reduce the separate 10-minute midday substitution ritual, spell scribing, rituals or spellbook reconstruction unless another feature explicitly says so.

source.originalText: Matrix Efficiency: Reduce the preparation time for spells by 25%.

cards.name: Floating Preparation
cards.effect: Floating Preparation. Tags: arch, passive, matrix. Increase your maximum prepared Spell Matrix count by 1. The extra matrix can come from any school and obeys all ordinary spellbook and rank restrictions. It is a prepared matrix for every rule, including protected strain, duplicate-family tracking and Matrix Mastery modifications.

source.originalText: Floating Preparation: Prepare 1 extra spell from any school each day

cards.name: Arcane Lock
cards.rangeAndTarget: One door, chest, portal or unattended object within touch
cards.effect: Arcane Lock. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, abjuration. Magically seal the target. Opening it without your permission requires a Strength check or thieves'/arcane-tool check against your Wizard spell DC. Dispel Magic can end the lock. You can designate up to M creatures who can bypass it. This does not make the object physically indestructible.

source.originalText: Arcane Lock: Create a magical barrier that prevents entry or access to an object or area.

cards.name: Scholarly Mind
cards.effect: Scholarly Mind. Tags: base, passive, knowledge. You have advantage on Intelligence checks whose primary purpose is recalling, researching or analyzing arcane theory, magical history, planar magical principles or constructed spell formulae. It does not grant advantage on spell attacks, Counterspell checks or general Investigation unrelated to arcane scholarship.

source.originalText: Scholarly Mind: Gain advantage on Intelligence checks related to arcane knowledge.

cards.name: Dispel Magic
cards.rangeAndTarget: One creature, object or magical effect within 60 feet
cards.effect: Dispel Magic. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, abjuration. Choose one ongoing spell effect you can perceive. If its rank is 3 or lower, end it. If it is rank 4 or higher, make an Intelligence check adding proficiency against DC 10 + spell rank; success ends it. Permanent artifact properties and effects explicitly immune to dispelling are unaffected.

source.originalText: Dispel Magic: End magical effects in an area or on a target.

cards.name: Arcane Sight
cards.effect: Arcane Sight. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, divination, concentration. While active you perceive magical auras within 60 feet and automatically know each visible aura's school or broad magical category. As an Action on a later turn, examine one aura to learn whether it is concentrated, summoned, cursed, warded or linked to another visible magical effect. Total cover blocks sight.

source.originalText: Arcane Sight: See magical auras and effects for a short duration.

cards.name: Dimensional Pocket
cards.effect: Dimensional Pocket. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, conjuration, ritual. Create an extradimensional storage space holding up to 100 pounds or 10 cubic feet of unattended nonliving material. Retrieving or placing an item while adjacent to the opening uses an object interaction. Living creatures cannot enter. When duration ends, remaining contents appear harmlessly in the nearest unoccupied space.

source.originalText: Dimensional Pocket: Create a small extradimensional space to store items.

cards.name: Analyze Magic
cards.rangeAndTarget: One magical creature, object or effect within 30 feet
cards.effect: Analyze Magic. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, divination, knowledge. Make an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 + the effect's spell rank, treating a non-spell effect's Director-assigned tier as rank. On success learn its school or magical category, one active mechanical property and whether it is currently sustained, cursed or bound to another effect. Failure reveals only that magic is present.

source.originalText: Analyze Magic: Study a magical effect or item to gain insight into its properties and function.

cards.name: Sigil Rewrite
cards.effect: Sigil Rewrite. Tags: arch, passive-upgrade, matrix. Replace one prepared matrix with a different spell from your spellbook of exactly the same rank without performing the normal 10-minute ritual. The replacement receives no special Dissonance reset for a matrix family already used this encounter and must obey current Wizard rank eligibility.

source.originalText: Sigil Rewrite: Once/day, instantly swap a spell you know for another of the same tier

cards.name: Spell Preservation
cards.effect: Spell Preservation. Tags: hero, spellbinder, passive, spellbook. Your primary spellbook cannot be destroyed, erased or rendered permanently unreadable by non-artifact mundane or magical means. It can still be stolen, hidden, transported, suppressed, sealed by an artifact-level effect or voluntarily abandoned. Copies and backup books do not automatically receive this protection.

source.originalText: Spell Preservation: Your spellbook cannot be destroyed by non-artifact means.

cards.name: Seal Magic
cards.effect: Seal Magic. Tags: hero, spellbinder, wizard-spell, control. Choose one of the eight schools and target one creature. It makes a Wisdom save. On failure it cannot cast spells of the chosen school. At the end of each of its turns it repeats the save, ending the Seal on success. The effect ends automatically after 3 rounds and never prevents non-spell class techniques merely because they are magical.

source.originalText: Seal Magic: Prevent a target from casting spells of a specific school (WIS save, 3 rounds)

cards.name: Arcane Shield
cards.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
cards.effect: Arcane Shield. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, abjuration, protection. Trigger when an attack roll would hit you. Gain +2 AC against the triggering attack and until the start of your next regular turn, potentially causing the attack to miss. Temporary AC from another Arcane Shield does not stack.

source.originalText: Arcane Shield: Create a barrier of magical force that provides temporary protection.

cards.name: Counterpulse
cards.rangeAndTarget: Caster whose spell you successfully Counterspelled
cards.duration: Until end of target's next turn
cards.effect: Counterpulse. Tags: hero, spellbinder, counter, control. Immediately after your Counterspell succeeds, spend 1 RP. The countered caster is Silenced until the end of its next turn. This is part of the successful counter event rather than another spell cast and cannot trigger another Counterpulse.

source.originalText: Counterpulse: Countering a spell silences the caster for 1 round

cards.name: Spellbook Study
cards.effect: Spellbook Study. Tags: base, active, matrix, ritual. Replace one currently prepared matrix with one legal spell recorded in your spellbook. The replacement must be within your Wizard rank limit. This is the normal midday substitution permission; it does not alter the spellbook, create another prepared-matrix position or reset first-cast/Refrain history for an underlying matrix family already cast this encounter.

source.originalText: Spellbook Study: Spend time studying your spellbook to prepare a different selection of spells.

automaticCards.name: Arcane Tradition
automaticCards.frequency: Automatic at Wizard 3; not a selection
automaticCards.effect: Arcane Tradition. Tags: arch, school, automatic. Your level-1 Arcane School becomes your Arcanist tradition; do not choose a second school. Prepare one additional matrix from that same school each day without counting it against your normal prepared-matrix maximum. It otherwise obeys all ordinary rank, spellbook, Dissonance and duplicate-family rules.

source.originalText: Arcane Tradition: Choose a school of magic to specialize in, gaining bonuses to spells of that school.

automaticCards.name: Counterspell
automaticCards.cost: 3 RP
automaticCards.rangeAndTarget: One creature you perceive casting a spell within 60 feet
automaticCards.effect: Counterspell. Tags: arch-source, automatic, wizard-spell, abjuration, disruption. Trigger when a creature begins casting a spell. This is gained automatically at Wizard 2 and is never also selected from the Arch pool.

source.originalText: Counterspell: Disrupt an enemy's spellcasting, potentially negating their spell entirely.

automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5186. This is the one School Mastery progression grant, not a second school choice or duplicate feat. Increase the level-1 Arcane School spell-attack and spell-save bonus from +1 to +2 total. Its school passive and bonus-spell rules otherwise remain unchanged.

source.originalText: | 5 | Bonus Feat: School Mastery |

automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5187. After preparing spells, choose one of acid, cold, fire, force, lightning, necrotic, psychic, radiant or thunder that is dealt by at least one prepared spell of your Arcane School. Gain resistance to that damage type until your next long rest. If none of your prepared school spells deals a damage type, choose force. This is provisional completion of the source's ambiguous 'chosen school's element' wording.

source.originalText: | 6 | Arcane Ward (resistance to chosen school's element) |

automaticCards.name: Dual Cast
automaticCards.cost: Pay the complete RP costs of both spells
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5188. Choose two DIFFERENT prepared Wizard spells of rank 1 or 2, neither of which summons a creature or grants an additional Action. Cast both sequentially as one Action, paying both RP costs. They cannot both require concentration. Each matrix separately updates first-cast/Refrain history. Features that trigger merely from 'casting a spell' may trigger once for each actual matrix unless that feature itself says once per turn; no trigger may create another Dual Cast or additional full Action.

source.originalText: | 9 | Dual Cast (cast 2 Tier 1–2 spells in a round) |

automaticCards.name: Overchannel
automaticCards.cost: Pay the Core V 2 RP cost for one rank above the spell's normal cast rank
automaticCards.rangeAndTarget: One prepared spell you are beginning to cast
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5190. Cast one prepared spell as though it were one rank higher than the highest rank at which you could normally cast that SAME spell, provided the spell has an explicit higher-rank scaling rule. Overchannel does not teach or prepare a higher-rank spell, cannot exceed effective rank 9 and cannot be combined with another generic Overcast rule during this pilot. All normal Dissonance/Refrain rules still apply.

completeEngine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Intelligence is the Wizard class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Wizard levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Intelligence modifier). Wizard spell attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier. Wizard spell save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier.

The Wizard remains three distinct stages: Base Wizard at levels 1-2, Arch Arcanist at levels 3-9, and one Hero path at levels 10-20: Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer. Hero paths are not additional starting classes and their features cannot be selected before their Wizard class-level gates.

SPELLBOOK. At Wizard 1 your spellbook contains six chosen rank-1 Wizard spells. Arcane School Specialization also adds one legal rank-1 bonus spell of your chosen school without replacing one of those six. For this provisional progression, add 2 legal Wizard spells to the book at each Wizard level 2-4, 3 at each level 5-8, 4 at each level 9-12, 5 at each level 13-16 and 6 at each level 17-20. Level-up additions cost no money or scribing time.

LEGAL RANKS. Maximum Wizard spell rank by Wizard class level is: rank 1 at levels 1-2, rank 2 at 3-4, rank 3 at 5-6, rank 4 at 7-8, rank 5 at 9-10, rank 6 at 11-12, rank 7 at 13-14, rank 8 at 15-16 and rank 9 at 17-20. Grand Tier at level 20 is a special casting permission, not a tenth ordinary rank. A Wizard may learn Wizard-list spells from any school up to the legal rank unless a spell itself has an additional prerequisite.

PREPARED SPELL MATRIX. After a long rest, prepare a number of matrices equal to Wizard level + Intelligence modifier, minimum 1, selecting only spells currently recorded in your spellbook and within your legal rank. You cast ordinary Wizard spells only from prepared matrices unless a feature explicitly overrides that restriction. Preparing the full daily matrix set normally requires 1 hour of spellbook study. Matrix Efficiency reduces this to 45 minutes.

DUPLICATE PREPARATION. You may prepare the same spell more than once, primarily to carry different Matrix Mastery configurations. Duplicate copies never create additional first-cast Dissonance exemptions. For Refrain and the protected strain rule, all prepared copies sharing the same underlying spell name belong to one matrix family regardless of modification.

MIDDAY SUBSTITUTION. Once between long rests, you may perform a 10-minute Spellbook Study ritual to replace one prepared matrix with another legal spell from your spellbook. The replacement cannot exceed your legal Wizard rank. Sigil Rewrite and Matrix Mastery may improve this process as explicitly stated.

SPELL ACQUISITION BY SCRIBING. A found Wizard spell may be copied into the spellbook if its rank is legal for you. Baseline scribing requires 2 hours and 50 gp of inks/materials per spell rank, treating rank 0 as 1 for this calculation. Spell Scribing halves both values to 1 hour and 25 gp per rank. Failure to finish the work consumes no spellbook entry but materials already expended during an interrupted hour are lost.

SPELLBOOK LOSS. Losing the spellbook does not erase matrices currently prepared in memory; you may continue casting those prepared matrices until you next rebuild or change preparation. A blank replacement book can be seeded with your currently prepared spells at 1 hour and 25 gp per effective spell rank each. An unprepared spell you previously recorded can be reconstructed from memory with 8 hours, 100 gp per rank and an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 + spell rank. Failure consumes that attempt's time and half its materials; another attempt can be made after a long rest. Recovering the original book automatically restores access to its surviving entries.

ARCANE SCHOOL SPECIALIZATION is automatic at Wizard 1. Choose exactly one of the eight schools. Your spell attacks with that school gain +1 and your Wizard save DC for that school's spells gains +1. You also add one legal rank-1 spell of that school to the spellbook. The source table explicitly supplies seven school passives; the eighth core school, Abjuration, is named elsewhere but its passive row is missing. Its provisional playtest passive is identified below rather than silently presented as recovered text.

ABJURATION, provisional completion for the omitted eighth row: once per round after you cast an Abjuration spell, gain temporary HP equal to PB until the start of your next regular turn. CONJURATION: creatures summoned by your Wizard spells gain +1 maximum HP per Wizard level. DIVINATION: once per long rest reroll one failed saving throw and use the new result. ENCHANTMENT: when a creature fails its initial save against one of your Enchantment spells, a printed control duration of at least 1 round may last one additional round, but every normally allowed repeat save still occurs. EVOCATION: when casting an area Evocation spell, exclude one creature from its initial damaging area; that creature automatically succeeds and takes no damage if success normally halves damage. ILLUSION: gain +2 on concentration saves made to maintain Illusion spells. NECROMANCY: once per turn during a real encounter when a hostile non-summoned creature dies from your Necromancy spell, gain 1 temporary HP; it is not permanent healing. TRANSMUTATION: after casting a Transmutation spell, gain +5 feet Speed until the end of that turn.

PROTECTED DISSONANCE INTERFACE. The first cast of each different prepared matrix family during an encounter generates 0 BASE Dissonance. This exemption affects only base strain. Refrain and explicitly printed strain costs still apply; the suite disables generic Overcast and does not layer historical Burn onto Dissonance. Repeating a matrix family follows normal Refrain immediately. Preparing duplicates or differently modified copies of the same underlying spell never refreshes the exemption.

Core Systems V 2 Resonance Points and spell-rank RP costs are authoritative for Wizard spellcasting. There are no historical spell slots in this pilot. Wizard cards tagged wizard-spell are always-prepared class matrices once acquired, do not consume a daily prepared-matrix position and use the same RP, concentration, Refrain and protected first-distinct-matrix rules as other Wizard spells. Their printed RP cost replaces any generic rank cost; never pay both.

RITUAL CASTING is automatic at Wizard 2. A Wizard spell in your spellbook with the Ritual tag can be cast from the book without being prepared by increasing its casting time by at least 10 minutes. A ritual cast costs 0 RP unless that ritual explicitly lists a consumed RP cost, cannot be used during an encounter and cannot generate or vent Dissonance through ordinary casting strain.

Only one concentration effect can normally be maintained. Starting a second concentration effect ends the first. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; required half-damage rounding is down for this pilot. Spell Tether and the level-17 Tethered Cast are the only Wizard-specific exceptions in this draft, and each has an explicit RP price, duration and one-tether cap.

MATRIX MASTERY MODIFICATIONS. After acquiring Matrix Mastery, each prepared ordinary spell matrix may carry at most one modification chosen during preparation. QUICK SUBSTITUTION: once per short rest, replace one matrix marked Quick Substitution with another spellbook spell of exactly the same rank using a 1-minute ritual instead of the normal 10-minute midday swap; the replacement loses the modification until the next long rest. COMPONENT ENHANCEMENT: when casting a damaging or healing matrix, spend 1 additional RP to add one extra die of the spell's primary damage or healing die to one roll; if the spell has no such die this modification has no effect. MATRIX LINKING: pair two different prepared matrix families during preparation; after legally casting one, the other costs 1 less RP, minimum 1, if cast before the end of your next regular turn, at most once per pair per round. STABILITY REINFORCEMENT: gain +2 on concentration saves caused by damage while maintaining that matrix. A matrix modification never creates another spell cast or proc event.

All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot grant another additional Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Spell copies, Matrix Sharing, Arcane Fusion, Dual Cast and similar effects pay all explicitly required RP and do not produce duplicate resource, cast-proc or action-grant chains beyond their written resolution.

Round recharge counters decrease once at the start of your regular initiative turn even if you cannot act. Extra Actions and extra turns do not tick recharge. Outside initiative, each uninterrupted 6 seconds counts as one tick. Only positive counters can be reset or shortened and each named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

SUMMON COMMAND LIMIT. All Wizard-controlled conjured, raised and bound companions share one damaging/control Companion Command per Wizard regular turn. Spend one Bonus Action to command exactly one such creature to move up to its Speed and use one damaging or control action from its stat block. Uncommanded creatures may reposition defensively and take Dodge but cannot deal damage or impose conditions. No summoned or raised creature can create XP, treasure, RP, Dissonance relief, additional corpses or kill-resource farms.

NECROMANCER STANDARD UNDEAD. Corpse Harvest and Auto-Raise share a maximum of three standard raised minions. Skeleton: AC 14, HP 6 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Bone Shot, range 30 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. Zombie: AC 12, HP 10 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 20; Slam, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. Goblin Thrall, available only from a goblinoid corpse: AC 13, HP 8 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Shiv, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. These are pre-Flesh-Ascendant statistics.

NECROMANCER AUTO-RAISE. Once per round when one of your standard undead minions personally lands the killing blow on an eligible humanoid and your standard-minion count is below three, its corpse rises at the end of the current turn as the same mechanical minion type that scored the kill, if physically possible. A new minion cannot act during that same round. Auto-Raise costs no Action or RP but can never exceed the three-minion cap or generate a new resource, corpse chain, XP or treasure event. Without Infernal Pact only humanoids qualify.

ELITE UNDEAD PETS. Necromancers may bind Boneflayer, Dreadblade and Wraithbound, at most one of each and three elite pets total. They use the same shared Companion Command limit as standard undead. Boneflayer: AC 14, HP 12 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Bone Shards: range 60, Wizard spell attack, 2d6+S necrotic. Fear Pulse replaces its attack: enemies within 10 feet make Wisdom saves; failure Frightened until end of next turn; recharge 3. Grave Miasma replaces its attack: 10-foot-radius point within 30 feet until start of your next turn; enemies entering or starting there take 1d6 necrotic once; recharge 3.

Dreadblade: AC 16, HP 16 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Disrupting Blade: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic; a concentrating target immediately makes its concentration save with disadvantage. On a natural 20 the target is Weakened until the end of its next turn, taking -1 on attack rolls. Dreadblade has advantage on saves against forced movement.

Wraithbound: AC 14, HP 10 + 2 × Wizard level, Fly 40 and hover. While it has not attacked or imposed control since the end of its previous turn it is Invisible; attacking ends that state until the end of its next turn. Wraith Strike: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. On natural 20 the target makes a Constitution save against your Wizard DC; failure Stuns until the end of its next turn.

Flesh Ascendant's bonus applies after the listed base statistics: every undead creature you control gains +2 maximum HP per Wizard level. If at least two of your undead creatures are active, each gains +1 AC and +1 on saving throws. This does not increase the standard-minion or elite-pet caps.

DARK-TRAUMA INTERFACE. Necromancer features involving corpse desecration, infernal bargains, domination, body control or Mind Prison remain subject to the project's existing dark-content and trauma boundaries. A table may fade description to black without changing mechanics. No feature changes a player's real belief, permanently transfers ownership of a player character or silently retires a PC.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Wizard 1 automatically gains Arcane School Specialization, Spell Matrix System and the starting spellbook, then chooses 4 selectable Base cards, at least 2 Active. Wizard 2 automatically gains Counterspell and Ritual Casting, then chooses 2 additional selectable Base cards. Counterspell is not also placed in the Arch selection pool.

At Wizard 3 enter Arcanist, automatically gain Arcane Tradition as an upgrade of the SAME level-1 school rather than choosing another school, and choose 2 selectable Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Wizard 4 grants one eligible Base/Arch choice. Wizard 5 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic School Mastery. Wizard 6 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic Arcane Ward. Wizard 7 grants one eligible Arch choice. Wizard 8 grants one Base/Arch choice. Wizard 9 grants one eligible Arch choice plus automatic Dual Cast.

At Wizard 10 choose Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer and gain 2 Hero cards from that path. ELEMENTALIST EXCEPTION: Elemental Affinity is automatic at path selection and counts as one of those two level-10 Hero acquisitions, so an Elementalist chooses only one additional Hero card at level 10. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. The chosen Final Theorem is automatic at Wizard 20. School Mastery, Counterspell, Arcane Tradition and all progression-table automatic features are never duplicated as selections.

All acquisition gates use Wizard class level rather than total character level. Normal proficiency bonus follows the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. A multiclass dip cannot unlock higher spell ranks, Arcanist cards, Hero cards, Final Theorems or progression-table features.

Class matrices tagged wizard-spell receive a rank in normalized card data equal to maximum ordinary Wizard rank at their minimum class-level gate (cap 9). Printed RP cost replaces generic rank cost. Counterspell is rank 1 at its explicit level 2 automatic grant. This explicit convention closes rank-dependent Counterspell/Dissonance interactions without inventing extra costs.

completeEngine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Intelligence is the Wizard class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Wizard levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Intelligence modifier). Wizard spell attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier. Wizard spell save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier.

The Wizard remains three distinct stages: Base Wizard at levels 1-2, Arch Arcanist at levels 3-9, and one Hero path at levels 10-20: Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer. Hero paths are not additional starting classes and their features cannot be selected before their Wizard class-level gates.

SPELLBOOK. At Wizard 1 your spellbook contains six chosen rank-1 Wizard spells. Arcane School Specialization also adds one legal rank-1 bonus spell of your chosen school without replacing one of those six. For this provisional progression, add 2 legal Wizard spells to the book at each Wizard level 2-4, 3 at each level 5-8, 4 at each level 9-12, 5 at each level 13-16 and 6 at each level 17-20. Level-up additions cost no money or scribing time.

LEGAL RANKS. Maximum Wizard spell rank by Wizard class level is: rank 1 at levels 1-2, rank 2 at 3-4, rank 3 at 5-6, rank 4 at 7-8, rank 5 at 9-10, rank 6 at 11-12, rank 7 at 13-14, rank 8 at 15-16 and rank 9 at 17-20. Grand Tier at level 20 is a special casting permission, not a tenth ordinary rank. A Wizard may learn Wizard-list spells from any school up to the legal rank unless a spell itself has an additional prerequisite.

PREPARED SPELL MATRIX. After a long rest, prepare a number of matrices equal to Wizard level + Intelligence modifier, minimum 1, selecting only spells currently recorded in your spellbook and within your legal rank. You cast ordinary Wizard spells only from prepared matrices unless a feature explicitly overrides that restriction. Preparing the full daily matrix set normally requires 1 hour of spellbook study. Matrix Efficiency reduces this to 45 minutes.

DUPLICATE PREPARATION. You may prepare the same spell more than once, primarily to carry different Matrix Mastery configurations. Duplicate copies never create additional first-cast Dissonance exemptions. For Refrain and the protected strain rule, all prepared copies sharing the same underlying spell name belong to one matrix family regardless of modification.

MIDDAY SUBSTITUTION. Once between long rests, you may perform a 10-minute Spellbook Study ritual to replace one prepared matrix with another legal spell from your spellbook. The replacement cannot exceed your legal Wizard rank. Sigil Rewrite and Matrix Mastery may improve this process as explicitly stated.

SPELL ACQUISITION BY SCRIBING. A found Wizard spell may be copied into the spellbook if its rank is legal for you. Baseline scribing requires 2 hours and 50 gp of inks/materials per spell rank, treating rank 0 as 1 for this calculation. Spell Scribing halves both values to 1 hour and 25 gp per rank. Failure to finish the work consumes no spellbook entry but materials already expended during an interrupted hour are lost.

SPELLBOOK LOSS. Losing the spellbook does not erase matrices currently prepared in memory; you may continue casting those prepared matrices until you next rebuild or change preparation. A blank replacement book can be seeded with your currently prepared spells at 1 hour and 25 gp per effective spell rank each. An unprepared spell you previously recorded can be reconstructed from memory with 8 hours, 100 gp per rank and an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 + spell rank. Failure consumes that attempt's time and half its materials; another attempt can be made after a long rest. Recovering the original book automatically restores access to its surviving entries.

ARCANE SCHOOL SPECIALIZATION is automatic at Wizard 1. Choose exactly one of the eight schools. Your spell attacks with that school gain +1 and your Wizard save DC for that school's spells gains +1. You also add one legal rank-1 spell of that school to the spellbook. The source table explicitly supplies seven school passives; the eighth core school, Abjuration, is named elsewhere but its passive row is missing. Its provisional playtest passive is identified below rather than silently presented as recovered text.

ABJURATION, provisional completion for the omitted eighth row: once per round after you cast an Abjuration spell, gain temporary HP equal to PB until the start of your next regular turn. CONJURATION: creatures summoned by your Wizard spells gain +1 maximum HP per Wizard level. DIVINATION: once per long rest reroll one failed saving throw and use the new result. ENCHANTMENT: when a creature fails its initial save against one of your Enchantment spells, a printed control duration of at least 1 round may last one additional round, but every normally allowed repeat save still occurs. EVOCATION: when casting an area Evocation spell, exclude one creature from its initial damaging area; that creature automatically succeeds and takes no damage if success normally halves damage. ILLUSION: gain +2 on concentration saves made to maintain Illusion spells. NECROMANCY: once per turn during a real encounter when a hostile non-summoned creature dies from your Necromancy spell, gain 1 temporary HP; it is not permanent healing. TRANSMUTATION: after casting a Transmutation spell, gain +5 feet Speed until the end of that turn.

PROTECTED DISSONANCE INTERFACE. The first cast of each different prepared matrix family during an encounter generates 0 BASE Dissonance. This exemption affects only base strain. Refrain and explicitly printed strain costs still apply; the suite disables generic Overcast and does not layer historical Burn onto Dissonance. Repeating a matrix family follows normal Refrain immediately. Preparing duplicates or differently modified copies of the same underlying spell never refreshes the exemption.

Core Systems V 2 Resonance Points and spell-rank RP costs are authoritative for Wizard spellcasting. There are no historical spell slots in this pilot. Wizard cards tagged wizard-spell are always-prepared class matrices once acquired, do not consume a daily prepared-matrix position and use the same RP, concentration, Refrain and protected first-distinct-matrix rules as other Wizard spells. Their printed RP cost replaces any generic rank cost; never pay both.

RITUAL CASTING is automatic at Wizard 2. A Wizard spell in your spellbook with the Ritual tag can be cast from the book without being prepared by increasing its casting time by at least 10 minutes. A ritual cast costs 0 RP unless that ritual explicitly lists a consumed RP cost, cannot be used during an encounter and cannot generate or vent Dissonance through ordinary casting strain.

Only one concentration effect can normally be maintained. Starting a second concentration effect ends the first. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; required half-damage rounding is down for this pilot. Spell Tether and the level-17 Tethered Cast are the only Wizard-specific exceptions in this draft, and each has an explicit RP price, duration and one-tether cap.

MATRIX MASTERY MODIFICATIONS. After acquiring Matrix Mastery, each prepared ordinary spell matrix may carry at most one modification chosen during preparation. QUICK SUBSTITUTION: once per short rest, replace one matrix marked Quick Substitution with another spellbook spell of exactly the same rank using a 1-minute ritual instead of the normal 10-minute midday swap; the replacement loses the modification until the next long rest. COMPONENT ENHANCEMENT: when casting a damaging or healing matrix, spend 1 additional RP to add one extra die of the spell's primary damage or healing die to one roll; if the spell has no such die this modification has no effect. MATRIX LINKING: pair two different prepared matrix families during preparation; after legally casting one, the other costs 1 less RP, minimum 1, if cast before the end of your next regular turn, at most once per pair per round. STABILITY REINFORCEMENT: gain +2 on concentration saves caused by damage while maintaining that matrix. A matrix modification never creates another spell cast or proc event.

All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot grant another additional Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Spell copies, Matrix Sharing, Arcane Fusion, Dual Cast and similar effects pay all explicitly required RP and do not produce duplicate resource, cast-proc or action-grant chains beyond their written resolution.

Round recharge counters decrease once at the start of your regular initiative turn even if you cannot act. Extra Actions and extra turns do not tick recharge. Outside initiative, each uninterrupted 6 seconds counts as one tick. Only positive counters can be reset or shortened and each named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

SUMMON COMMAND LIMIT. All Wizard-controlled conjured, raised and bound companions share one damaging/control Companion Command per Wizard regular turn. Spend one Bonus Action to command exactly one such creature to move up to its Speed and use one damaging or control action from its stat block. Uncommanded creatures may reposition defensively and take Dodge but cannot deal damage or impose conditions. No summoned or raised creature can create XP, treasure, RP, Dissonance relief, additional corpses or kill-resource farms.

NECROMANCER STANDARD UNDEAD. Corpse Harvest and Auto-Raise share a maximum of three standard raised minions. Skeleton: AC 14, HP 6 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Bone Shot, range 30 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. Zombie: AC 12, HP 10 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 20; Slam, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. Goblin Thrall, available only from a goblinoid corpse: AC 13, HP 8 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Shiv, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. These are pre-Flesh-Ascendant statistics.

NECROMANCER AUTO-RAISE. Once per round when one of your standard undead minions personally lands the killing blow on an eligible humanoid and your standard-minion count is below three, its corpse rises at the end of the current turn as the same mechanical minion type that scored the kill, if physically possible. A new minion cannot act during that same round. Auto-Raise costs no Action or RP but can never exceed the three-minion cap or generate a new resource, corpse chain, XP or treasure event. Without Infernal Pact only humanoids qualify.

ELITE UNDEAD PETS. Necromancers may bind Boneflayer, Dreadblade and Wraithbound, at most one of each and three elite pets total. They use the same shared Companion Command limit as standard undead. Boneflayer: AC 14, HP 12 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Bone Shards: range 60, Wizard spell attack, 2d6+S necrotic. Fear Pulse replaces its attack: enemies within 10 feet make Wisdom saves; failure Frightened until end of next turn; recharge 3. Grave Miasma replaces its attack: 10-foot-radius point within 30 feet until start of your next turn; enemies entering or starting there take 1d6 necrotic once; recharge 3.

Dreadblade: AC 16, HP 16 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Disrupting Blade: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic; a concentrating target immediately makes its concentration save with disadvantage. On a natural 20 the target is Weakened until the end of its next turn, taking -1 on attack rolls. Dreadblade has advantage on saves against forced movement.

Wraithbound: AC 14, HP 10 + 2 × Wizard level, Fly 40 and hover. While it has not attacked or imposed control since the end of its previous turn it is Invisible; attacking ends that state until the end of its next turn. Wraith Strike: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. On natural 20 the target makes a Constitution save against your Wizard DC; failure Stuns until the end of its next turn.

Flesh Ascendant's bonus applies after the listed base statistics: every undead creature you control gains +2 maximum HP per Wizard level. If at least two of your undead creatures are active, each gains +1 AC and +1 on saving throws. This does not increase the standard-minion or elite-pet caps.

DARK-TRAUMA INTERFACE. Necromancer features involving corpse desecration, infernal bargains, domination, body control or Mind Prison remain subject to the project's existing dark-content and trauma boundaries. A table may fade description to black without changing mechanics. No feature changes a player's real belief, permanently transfers ownership of a player character or silently retires a PC.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Wizard 1 automatically gains Arcane School Specialization, Spell Matrix System and the starting spellbook, then chooses 4 selectable Base cards, at least 2 Active. Wizard 2 automatically gains Counterspell and Ritual Casting, then chooses 2 additional selectable Base cards. Counterspell is not also placed in the Arch selection pool.

At Wizard 3 enter Arcanist, automatically gain Arcane Tradition as an upgrade of the SAME level-1 school rather than choosing another school, and choose 2 selectable Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Wizard 4 grants one eligible Base/Arch choice. Wizard 5 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic School Mastery. Wizard 6 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic Arcane Ward. Wizard 7 grants one eligible Arch choice. Wizard 8 grants one Base/Arch choice. Wizard 9 grants one eligible Arch choice plus automatic Dual Cast.

At Wizard 10 choose Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer and gain 2 Hero cards from that path. ELEMENTALIST EXCEPTION: Elemental Affinity is automatic at path selection and counts as one of those two level-10 Hero acquisitions, so an Elementalist chooses only one additional Hero card at level 10. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. The chosen Final Theorem is automatic at Wizard 20. School Mastery, Counterspell, Arcane Tradition and all progression-table automatic features are never duplicated as selections.

All acquisition gates use Wizard class level rather than total character level. Normal proficiency bonus follows the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. A multiclass dip cannot unlock higher spell ranks, Arcanist cards, Hero cards, Final Theorems or progression-table features.

Class matrices tagged wizard-spell receive a rank in normalized card data equal to maximum ordinary Wizard rank at their minimum class-level gate (cap 9). Printed RP cost replaces generic rank cost. Counterspell is rank 1 at its explicit level 2 automatic grant. This explicit convention closes rank-dependent Counterspell/Dissonance interactions without inventing extra costs.

Cantrip completion: know 3 Wizard cantrips at 1, 4 at 4, 5 at 10, using the shared missing-repertoire fallback. Cantrips are known directly and do not consume prepared matrices. Always-prepared class matrices are additional cards, not extra arbitrary ordinary spells. Class spell ranks and the normalized activation field resolve incomplete source terminology.
T.optionalChoicesInCases: No Matrix Mastery, Spell Efficiency, Improved Concentration, Sigil Authority or Knowledge Shield acquired. Dual Cast, Overchannel, class Arcane Shield and optional Counterpulse are not invoked unless expressly declared. No Arcane Feedback at13.
T.profileScope: An explicitly supplied finite class-built teaching creature profile using the complete actual class engine/cards. Not a newly rated bestiary creature, not authenticated campaign or ancestry acquisition, and not permission to fill an absent future profile.
T.checks: Use current ability modifier and actual acquired named card when applicable; save proficiency is not an ability-check proficiency. No Athletics proficiency is claimed.
T.actualActionsAvailable: Each annotated actual regular START supplies the normal Action/BonusAction/Reaction/movement according to the real source; the event trace explicitly consumes each used budget. No extra action source is assumed.

For Pyroclasm, select C as the one initial-area excluded recipient. Targeted Arcbolt arcs are a selected creature list, not an all-creature damaging area; no extra damage recipient or exclusion is inferred from its shared pool. Actual optional acquired Arcane Shield/Counterpulse and automatic Dual Cast/Overchannel are declined in these cases, not falsely called unacquired. No Arcane Feedback before14. No additional feat.

Level1 bonus uses actual Evocation Burning Hands, not Conjuration Elemental Bolt.
Prepared families and Arcane Ward explicitly updated; all recorded acquired class cards remain.

H.kind: Source-qualified illustrative character, not a verified campaign actor or rated monster

focus-pack.contents: real ordinary wooden focus and mundane personal carrying effects; no consumed materials/charged item; gross figures include every item once
focus-pack.custody: physically carried; reusable focus held with usable hands; light ordinary clothing, no armor surcharge or consumed material.

bookAndPreparation.unlistedAllowance: All unspecified book additions unused for these fixtures; these assignments fit their actual per-level limits.
